Executive Summary
This study presents an analysis of three-particle azimuthal correlations in proton-proton (pp), deuteron-gold (d+Au), and gold-gold (Au+Au) collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of 200 GeV, utilizing data from the STAR experiment. The research focuses on identifying signatures of Mach cone shock waves generated by high-energy partons traversing the quark-gluon plasma (QGP). By analyzing correlations between a high-momentum trigger particle (3 < pT < 4 GeV/c) and two softer associated particles (1 < pT < 2 GeV/c), the authors investigate the away-side structure of jet-like correlations. The analysis employs a rigorous background subtraction method to isolate genuine three-particle signals from combinatorial backgrounds arising from flow harmonics and uncorrelated particle production. Key findings include the observation of off-diagonal peaks in central Au+Au collisions at an angle of approximately 1.45 radians relative to the trigger, which is consistent with conical emission. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the emission angle remains constant across different associated particle transverse momenta, a result that distinguishes hydrodynamic Mach cone emission from alternative mechanisms like QCD-Cherenkov radiation, which would predict a momentum-dependent angle. The robustness of the signal against variations in flow harmonic measurements and normalization windows confirms the reliability of the observation, suggesting the presence of Mach cones in the heavy ion collision medium.

Research Context
Heavy ion collisions create a medium that may be the quark gluon plasma. This medium can be studied through jets and jet-correlations. Two-particle jet-like azimuthal correlations have shown the away-side shape in central Au+Au collisions to be broadened with respect to pp and peripheral Au+Au collisions or even double humped. The away-side structure is consistent with many different physics mechanisms including: large angle gluon radiation, jets deflected by radial flow or preferential selection of particles due to path-length dependent energy loss, hydrodynamic conical flow generated by Mach-cone shock waves, and Čerenkov radiation. Three-particle correlations can be used to differentiate conical flow and Čerenkov radiation, which have the characteristic of conical emission, from other mechanisms. In addition, the associated particle pT dependence of the conical emission angle can be used to differentiate between hydrodynamic conical flow and simple Čerenkov radiation.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study investigates whether off-diagonal structures in three-particle correlations indicate the presence of Mach-cone shock waves in the QGP. The analysis aims to distinguish between hydrodynamic conical flow and simple QCD-Čerenkov radiation based on the angular position of the signal. A key hypothesis is that the emission angle of Mach cone radiation is independent of the associated particle momentum, unlike Čerenkov radiation. The study predicts that off-diagonal peaks will appear at a specific angle (approx 1.45 radians) in central collisions if conical emission is present. The researchers hypothesize that the signal will be robust against variations in flow harmonic subtraction methods.

Methodological Details
The data were all taken in the STAR time projection chamber for pp, d+Au and Au+Au collisions at √sNN=200 GeV/c. The results reported here are for charged trigger particles of 3 < pT < 4 GeV/c and two charged associated particles of 1 < pT < 2 GeV/c. The analysis is performed by treating the events as composed of two components, particles that are jet-like correlated with the trigger particle and background particles. One source of background, the hard-soft background, results when one of the associated particles has a jet-like correlation with the trigger particle and the other is uncorrelated. The background is constructed from the 2-particle jet-like correlation, ˆJ2, folded with the normalized 2-particle background, Binc2. The 2-particle background is constructed by mixing events with the flow modulation added in pairwise from the average v2 values from the measurements based on the reaction plane and 4-particle cumulant methods. For the v4 contribution we use the parameterization v4 = 1.15v22 from the data. The background is normalized (with scale factor α) to the signal within 0.8 < |∆φ| < 1.2 (zero yield at 1 radian or ZYA1). Another source of background, the soft-soft background, results from correlations between the two associated particles which are independent of the trigger particle. This background is obtained from mixed events, where the trigger particle and the associated particles are from different events in the same centrality window. The trigger flow is added in triplet-wise from mixed events, where the trigger and associated particles are all from different events in the same centrality window. The total background is then, ˆJ2 ⊗αBinc2 + βα2(Binc3 + Binc,TF3). The normalization α2 corrects for the multiplicity bias from requiring a trigger particle.

Procedures And Architectures
Figure 1b shows the raw 3-particle azimuthal distribution in ∆φaT = φa −φT and ∆φbT = φb −φT. Combinatorial backgrounds must be removed to obtain the genuine 3-particle correlation signal. The off-diagonal signals were determined from a double Gaussian fit to a strip projected to the off-diagonal. The locations of the off-diagonal signals were found to be 1.45 radians from π. Figure 5 (left) shows the dependence the off-diagonal peak angle on associated particle pT. The angle is consistent with constant as a function of associated particle pT. Figure 5 (right) shows the centrality dependence the off-diagonal peak angle. The angle is consistent with remaining constant as a function of centrality for mid-central and central Au+Au collisions. The solid line at 1.46 on the plot is from a fit to a constant. The default v2 used is the average those measured by the reaction plane and 4-particle cumulant methods. We use the reaction plane and 4-particle cumulant v2 as the upper and lower bounds to estimate the systematic uncertainty of the v2 subtraction. To study the effect of the normalization the size of the normalization window was doubled to 0.6 < |∆φ| < 1.4. The signal is robust with respect to this change in normalization.

Key Results
Peaks are clearly visible for the near-side, (0,0), the away-side, (π,π) and the two cases of one particle on the near-side and the other on the away-side. The away-side peak displays diagonal elongation that is consistent with kT broadening. The more central Au+Au collisions display an off-diagonal structure, at about π ± 1.45 radians, that is consistent with conical emission. The structure increases in magnitude with centrality and is prominent in the high statistics top 12% central data provided by the on-line ZDC trigger. The off-diagonal signals (circle) increase with centrality and significantly deviate from zero in central Au+Au collisions. Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The off-diagonal structure ... is consistent with conical emission. The dependence of the observed signal angular position on the pT of the associated particles can be used to distinguish conical flow from simple QCD-Čerenkov radiation. The Mach cone emission angle is expected to be independent of the associated particle momentum, while the Čerenkov radiation model predicts an emission angle that is sharply decreasing with increasing associated particle momentum. No strong pT dependence of the angles on associated particle pT is observed. This result is consistent with Mach cone emission. Additional on-diagonal broadening has been seen in Au+Au collisions possibly due to deflected jets. The analysis treats events as the sum of two components, particles that are jet-like correlated with the trigger and background particles.

Other sources of systematic error include the effect on the trigger particle flow from requiring a correlated particle (20% on trigger particle v2). Uncertainty in the v4 parameterization ... and multiplicity bias effects on the soft-soft background.
